scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4630: One of our IT lab machines (the one called it_lab3)
has dropped off the network completely -- from that machine you cannot reach
anything at all, not even the first thing it is supposed to talk to. The
other machines around it are all fine; it is just that one. The student who
uses it did not change anything, so stop looking at our end. Someone here
has already called it: its port died. I couldn't tell you what a port is,
but it is your equipment, and one machine does not cut itself off. Find out
why that one machine is cut off and put it back on today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. it_lab3 has its IP on 192.168.1.0/24, reaches its
  gateway (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss, and RIP is converged so it reaches other
  segments too. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a single-host isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- it_lab3 is totally isolated
and cannot reach even its gateway -- is NOT reproducible: it_lab3 holds its
192.168.1.0/24 address, reaches its default gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss, and
(RIP being converged on router0/router1/router2) reaches off-segment destinations as
well.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: it_lab3 is fully connected and the user's
report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the it_lab3 -> gateway path
(and an off-segment ping), finds it working, checks the host's interface/route, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead port or isolated host to satisfy the
ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text: A thorough multi-layer investigation of it_lab3 and its network path found no fault, past or present. Phase 1 reachability confirmed 0 % loss across all sampled host pairs. Direct probes on it_lab3 showed its eth0 interface is UP/LOWER_UP with a correctly assigned address (192.168.1.5/24) and a valid default route (via 192.168.1.1). The machine successfully pinged its gateway, its LAN peers (it_lab1, it_lab2), and remote destinations across three separate IP segments (servers at 1.0.0.5, internet at 128.168.0.x, office at 192.168.3.2), all at 0 % loss. The l2_snapshot confirmed no duplicate MACs and no down or missing interfaces on any of the 30 lab devices, including it_lab3. The infra_sweep found no ACL drop rules, no static ARP poisoning, and no addressing divergence. The tc_snapshot showed every interface carries only the default fq_codel qdisc — no bandwidth throttling or corruption shaping. The link counter for eth0 on it_lab3 records zero errors, zero dropped packets, and — critically — zero carrier changes, meaning the physical link has never toggled since lab start. journalctl returns "No entries," confirming no historical network events were logged. No flap, stress, or flood processes were found running on the device. The dhcp_link_history and pressure_sweep were both clean. The reported symptom — complete isolation, unable to reach even the first hop — cannot be reproduced and leaves no mechanism or historical trace. Root cause: the claimed outage is unconfirmed; all evidence is consistent with a continuously healthy device. No corrective action is warranted from the network infrastructure side.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes it_lab3 holds its address and reaches its gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly states it_lab3 has 192.168.1.5/24 and successfully pings its gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss, confirming baseline health.

The agent's investigation log contains direct, instrumented observations (ip addr, ip route, ip link, pings to gateway, LAN peers, and off‑segment hosts, plus infra/l2/tc/dhcp snapshots) that support the writeup. The conclusions follow logically from those observations and the checks cover the necessary layers to rule out a network-side fault.
